scope: Read-only independent review of CloudZao branding, chronology, firmware source identities, release snapshots and update policy. Main tree was not modified. Review observed an actively edited tree.

findings.observed: Both new GitHub watch entries use /releases as metadataUrl. Current validator and releaseRequest require /releases/latest. Calling updateFirmwareCatalog throws Invalid GitHub metadata source before updates can be evaluated.
findings.suggestedFix: Use /releases/latest as the configured metadataUrl; releaseHistoryLimit already requests /releases?per_page=20. Retain the exact fetched source URL in historical snapshot evidence.
findings.verifiedRemedy: Without writing files, replaced those two values in an in-memory object. updateFirmwareCatalog then retained all five CloudZao selected firmware entries and returned unchanged catalog.

findings.observed: The two Claw compatibility notes still state only release metadata was checked and firmware bodies were not inspected. The selected catalog assets now have a successful RAM-only static audit.
findings.suggestedFix: State that selected digest-pinned artifacts passed static integrity/layout checks, without startup/function/hardware verification; future candidates do not inherit that audit.

findings.observed: INK4 and INK4 Plus CAD search objects say officialMechanicalModelFound:false although the existing catalog has manufacturer MakerWorld STL/STEP with preserved license and byte receipts. The scoped repository search is valid but broad field naming can be misread as global absence.
findings.suggestedFix: Name the negative field repositoryMechanicalModelFound and add knownExistingManufacturerCad references to the existing official MakerWorld CAD, or mark officialMechanicalModelFound:true for those two models.

findings.observed: Claw4 selected asset has sourcePolicy:immutable-pinned. Original public GitHub release response has immutable:false for v2.0.5.1 as well as the other releases. The version tag and hash pin the accepted content, but do not make the upstream release immutable.
findings.suggestedFix: Use mutable-pinned with the existing SHA256 and retain the precise version-tag-and-sha256-pinned identity description already in firmwares.json.

findings.observed: These snapshots were generated at 17:18 before the 17:20 RAM audit and correctly describe that earlier observation. Without an explicit phase label, their binaryFetched:false and no-bodies-downloaded storagePolicy look contradictory beside the later report.
findings.suggestedFix: Label them pre-download metadata snapshots and point to the later memory audit; keep their original check times and source metadata unchanged.

verified: Existing metalio-ink4 and metalio-ink4-plus IDs, runtime objects and defaultFirmwareIds are byte-equivalent JSON values to baseline. All three existing INK source URLs, SHA256, versions, status, verification flags, catalogUpdate and history remain unchanged.
All four current product manufacturers are CloudZao. Searching CloudZao, Metalio, Nologo or the prior Chinese brand finds all four. Order is Claw 1.54, INK4 Plus, INK4, Claw4.
Chronology dates match earliest reachable commits and remain explicitly low-confidence repository proxies rather than sale dates.

Selected Claw URLs, expected sizes, SHA256, release IDs, asset IDs and tag identities match the independent release metadata and RAM-only audit. Claw4 release v2.0.5.1 separately preserves actual app descriptor 2.0.5; Claw 1.54 preserves mutable latest/datefilename/hash identity.
Both selected Claw firmwares remain trial, role:official, simulationVerified:false and hardwareValidated:false. No proof of factory-preinstalled version is claimed.
Claw4 product has board:null/unavailable and display implemented:false. Firmware documentation separately states unavailable P4 MIPI board runtime and online flasher policy.
Both Claw watch entries have catalogTargets:[], which causes no-explicit-device-targets and leaves selected files unchanged after the URL configuration remedy.
INK4 2.0.79 and Plus 2.0.83 candidates have no publisher SHA256; the pure update function returns candidate-missing-sha256 and retains earlier selected artifacts and verification.

Release snapshot assets match upstream metadata; Claw4 latest August snapshot is correctly distinct from the July version-tag default. No raw uploader/account fields were introduced in public evidence.

57 path-addressable source receipts and the Burner registry HTML have matching original byte lengths and SHA256 in local research cache. Burner official API raw bytes were intentionally discarded after a white-listed representation; its original receipt remains explicit about that distinction.
Copied tools/audit-cloudzao-firmware.py matches the audit report reproducer SHA256 c408a90cf235c7167a11c1935187116d47d9140ea3985009f163f060edc7f81e.
runtimeLimit: No additional official firmware download, execution, hardware test or browser CORS test was performed during this review.

integrationResolution.githubAdapter: Both Claw metadata URLs now use /releases/latest; releaseHistoryLimit=5 preserves history discovery. Original snapshot sourceUrl retains the actual list URL fetched.
integrationResolution.staticAuditWording: Catalog/watchlist distinguish static integrity, bounded official boot and full functionality.
integrationResolution.mutableRelease: Both watch assets use mutable-pinned with SHA-256; fixed version tag is not a GitHub immutable release claim.
integrationResolution.existingCad: INK entries name retained manufacturer MakerWorld CAD and original attribution.
integrationResolution.stageNote: Discovery snapshot is explicitly dated before the subsequent audit/probe.
